title: Realtek or other onboard audio driver stopped working (Code 10 or no output device) after an update
symptoms: Sound stopped working right after a Windows Update or a driver update
Device Manager shows a yellow warning on the audio device with "This device cannot start. (Code 10)"
The sound icon says "No audio output device is installed"
causes: A newer audio driver delivered by Windows Update or the PC maker is not compatible with this PC
The audio driver package is damaged or only partly installed
A generic or other vendor's Realtek driver replaced the PC maker's customized driver

signals: A device in the MEDIA class (for example Realtek(R) Audio or High Definition Audio Device) has a problem status such as Code 10
No active playback endpoints exist although an onboard audio device is present
The audio driver date or version changed recently, and Roll Back Driver is available

fixes.title: Roll back the audio driver to the previous version
steps: Open Device Manager.
Expand Sound, video and game controllers.
Right-click the audio device (for example Realtek(R) Audio) and select Properties.
Select the Driver tab, then select Roll Back Driver. This button is available only if an earlier driver is stored on the PC.
Restart the PC and test the sound.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft support article; Roll Back Driver listed as fix when audio broke after an update
Official Microsoft troubleshooting page, step 9: roll back if audio worked before Windows Update
Microsoft Q&A answers giving the same rollback and uninstall steps; asker reports rollback replaced the driver (not marked accepted)

fixes.title: Uninstall the audio device and let Windows reinstall the driver
steps: Open Device Manager and expand Sound, video and game controllers.
Right-click the audio device and select Uninstall device.
On Windows 11, select the Attempt to remove the driver for this device check box. On Windows 10, select Delete the driver software for this device. Then select Uninstall.
Restart the PC. Windows reinstalls an audio driver automatically.
If the device does not come back, open Device Manager and select Action > Scan for hardware changes.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft troubleshooting page, step 9: uninstall with driver removal, restart to reinstall
Microsoft Q&A answer: uninstall with delete driver software, then Scan for hardware changes
Dell Community thread marked Solved: uninstall with delete driver software, restart, then install Dell's Realtek driver; several users report audio restored

fixes.title: Install the audio driver package from the PC or motherboard maker
steps: Find the exact model of the PC, laptop, or motherboard.
Go to the maker's support site (for example Dell, HP, Lenovo, ASUS, MSI) and download the audio driver for that model and Windows version.
Run the maker's installer as administrator and follow the instructions.
Restart the PC and test the sound.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft Device Manager error code reference: for Code 10, update the driver or download the latest driver from the hardware vendor
Intel support article: generic driver versions may be incompatible with OEM-customized systems; use drivers from the OEM
Dell Community thread marked Solved; accepted reply and other users restored audio by installing Dell's Realtek driver

fixes.title: Switch to the generic Microsoft High Definition Audio Device driver
steps: Open Device Manager and expand Sound, video and game controllers.
Right-click the audio device and select Update driver.
Select Browse my computer for drivers, then Let me pick from a list of available drivers on my computer.
Select High Definition Audio Device, then select Next. Accept the compatibility warning if one appears.
Restart the PC and test the sound. Note: vendor apps such as Realtek Audio Console and OEM sound effects stop working with the generic driver.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft troubleshooting page, step 9: try the generic audio driver that comes with Windows (High Definition Audio Device)
Microsoft Tech Community reply giving the same steps and warning not to force an incompatible driver (no user confirmation)

title: Intel Smart Sound Technology (SST) audio controller shows Code 10 and there is no sound
symptoms: No sound on a laptop after a system, driver, or BIOS update
Device Manager > System devices shows Intel(R) Smart Sound Technology (Intel(R) SST) Audio Controller or Intel SST OED with a yellow warning and Code 10
The sound icon says "No audio output device is installed"
causes: The Intel SST driver does not match the Realtek or Conexant audio driver and the BIOS shipped by the PC maker
A generic Intel SST driver was installed over the PC maker's customized driver

signals: A System-class device named Intel(R) Smart Sound Technology (Intel(R) SST) Audio Controller or Intel(R) Smart Sound Technology (Intel(R) SST) OED has problem code 10
No onboard playback endpoint is present

fixes.title: Install the matching Intel SST and audio drivers from the PC maker
steps: Find the exact model of the laptop.
Go to the PC maker's support site and download the audio driver package and, if listed, the Intel SST driver and latest BIOS for that model.
Install the BIOS update first if one is offered, then the Intel SST driver, then the audio driver, following the maker's instructions.
Restart the PC and test the sound.
If no matching driver is available, contact the PC maker's support.

sources.signal: Intel support article for Code 10/Code 31 after SST update: get drivers from the OEM
Microsoft release health: install newer Intel SST Audio Controller drivers via Windows Update or from the device maker
Dell Community thread marked Solved: Dell's Realtek driver package cleared the SST Code 10 for several users

fixes.title: Switch the Intel SST Audio Controller to the generic High Definition Audio Controller driver
steps: Open Device Manager and expand System devices.
Right-click Intel(R) Smart Sound Technology (Intel(R) SST) Audio Controller and select Update driver.
Select Browse my computer for drivers, then Let me pick from a list of available drivers on my computer.
Select High Definition Audio Controller and install it.
Restart the PC and test the sound. If the SST OED device still shows Code 10, install the PC maker's driver package instead.

sources.signal: Intel support article: no audio with Code 10 on Intel SST after a system, driver, or BIOS update; fix is selecting High Definition Audio Controller
Dell Community thread: original poster reports selecting High Definition Audio Controller fixed both affected Latitude laptops

title: Blue screen or blocked Windows 11 upgrade caused by Intel SST driver 10.29.0.5152 or 10.30.0.5152
symptoms: A PC with an Intel 11th Gen Core processor shows a blue screen on Windows 11
Windows Update does not offer the Windows 11 upgrade on a Windows 10 PC with an 11th Gen Intel processor
causes: Intel Smart Sound Technology Audio Controller driver IntcAudioBus.sys version 10.29.0.5152 or 10.30.0.5152 is incompatible with Windows 11

signals: The device Intel(R) Smart Sound Technology (Intel(R) SST) Audio Controller uses IntcAudioBus.sys with file version 10.29.0.5152 or 10.30.0.5152
The processor is an Intel 11th Gen Core

fixes.title: Update the Intel SST driver to version 10.29.00.5714 / 10.30.00.5714 or later
steps: Open Settings > Windows Update and select Check for updates. Install any driver updates offered.
If no newer Intel SST driver is offered, download the Intel SST Audio Controller driver for your model from the PC maker's support site and install it.
Restart the PC.
Check in Device Manager > System devices that the Intel SST Audio Controller driver version is 10.29.00.5714 or later, or 10.30.00.5714 or later.
Wait up to 48 hours for the Windows 11 upgrade to be offered. Do not force the upgrade before the driver is updated.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft release health known issue (Resolved External, 2024-04-12) with affected and fixed versions
Intel support article: get Intel SST driver updates from the OEM because generic versions may be incompatible
